questions.title: Why does 	extsf{FeatLLM} fix the number of rules per class to 10 instead of letting the LLM decide?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that the prompt is forced to return exactly 10 rules per class. I understand this helps control prompt size, but how does this limitation affect the quality of the rules? Could a different number of rules change performance significantly, and why was 10 chosen as the sweet spot?

questions.title: How exactly does the two‑step reasoning instruction prevent learning spurious correlations?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.1, the authors split reasoning into (1) inferring causal relationships from prior knowledge and (2) using that knowledge with few‑shot examples to produce class‑specific rules. I still don’t see how this guarantees that irrelevant columns won’t appear in a rule. Wouldn’t the LLM still generate a rule using an unrelated feature if it sees a spurious pattern in the demonstrations?

questions.title: What is the role of the non‑negative constraint on weights $	ext{max}( oldsymbol{w}_k,0)$ in Eq.(1)?
questions.question_body: Equation (1) projects each weight vector onto the non‑negative orthant before computing logits. The text says this ensures that feature generation does not ‘reduce’ class likelihood. However, I’m unsure why negative weights could hurt performance, and whether enforcing positivity might lose useful discriminatory information.

questions.title: How does bagging over features versus bagging over instances differ in practice?
questions.question_body: "Bagging” is said to mitigate prompt size limits by sampling features or instances per trial, but the paper doesn’t clearly distinguish these two schemes. Does picking fewer features reduce prompt length more effectively than picking fewer instances, and how do we decide which dimension to bootstrap?

questions.title: Why is 	extsf{FeatLLM} evaluated only on classification tasks and not regression?
questions.question_body: The method produces binary rule–derived features and then learns a linear classifier over them. Could this framework extend to regression problems (e.g., predicting continuous outcomes)? If so, what changes would be necessary in rule extraction or loss computation?

questions.title: What are potential failure modes when LLM-generated rules contain syntax errors?
questions.question_body: The paper obtains parsing code from an LLM to convert natural‑language rules into executable predicates. If the LLM introduces subtle syntactic inconsistencies (e.g., missing brackets or quoting issues), how robust is the parsing pipeline? What error‑handling mechanisms exist?

questions.title: "Rule similarity" measurement: How are we guaranteed that repeating ensembles actually produce diverse rules?
questions.question_body: "Self‑consistency" analysis (Appendix) says commonly inferred rules across trials indicate reliability. But I don’t see a quantitative metric for rule diversity among different ensembles. Is there an empirical test we can run to confirm that each ensemble learns distinct rule subsets?

questions.title: "Prior knowledge from feature descriptions" – Are these descriptions mandatory for all datasets?
questions.question_body: For datasets where feature names are concise or ambiguous, can we still use 	extsf{FeatLLM}? The method relies on having natural language descriptions and definitions for each feature; what happens if such metadata is missing?

questions.title: 'Feature bagging' vs 'instance bagging': what is their effect on few-shot sample size?

" Feature bagging" reduces prompt length by subsampling features; "instance bagging" subsamples training examples. In low‑shot regimes (e.g., k=4), do we lose critical information by dropping examples? How do we balance the two when k is very small?
